brief.from: The sorted list of 65 characters exists, but a model needs each character tied to a number, and a way back from number to character.

beats.idea: Encoding means giving each character the number of its position in the sorted list, so the list order becomes the id.
beats.shows: Pick the first characters of the printed list and read off their ids by position: newline 0, space 1, '!' 2.

beats.idea: stoi is a dictionary built by enumerate(chars), which yields (position, character) pairs, flipped into character:position.
beats.shows: Write out by hand what stoi['a'] and stoi['!'] look up, using the sorted order from the printed list.

beats.idea: itos is the same enumerate pairs kept as position:character, which is the exact reverse table.
beats.shows: Compare lines 30 and 31 side by side: only the order of ch and i in the comprehension differs.

beats.idea: encode looks up every character of a string in stoi and returns a list of ints; decode looks up every id in itos and joins them into a string.
beats.shows: Trace encode('hi') to two ids and decode back to 'hi'; round trip returns the original string.

beats.idea: The mapping only covers the 65 seen characters, so an unseen one raises an error, and both dictionaries are saved in the meta file for later reuse.
beats.shows: Predict what encoding 'é' does, and find where both dictionaries are stored in meta.

brief.to: With encode ready, the text can be cut into training and validation parts, starting with the ninety percent split.
